titles: 15 Thanksgiving Things We All Did in the 1970s — Unthinkable Today
Thanksgiving in the 1970s: 15 Things Only People Over 60 Remember
15 Thanksgiving Rituals From the 1970s Your Grandkids Won't Believe
description_intro:
Thanksgiving 1970s memories, the whole day, hour by hour: the turkey sliding into the oven before sunrise, the parade on the big console TV, and Santa's sleigh telling us Christmas could finally begin.

We'll put on our Sunday best, pile into the station wagon for the long drive to Grandma's, and watch Dad carve with that buzzing electric knife. There's gelatin salad, ridged canned cranberry, ashtrays on the coffee table, and Dad snoring in the recliner through the fourth quarter. And of course, the kids' table.

Which of these did your family do? Tell us where you grew up in the comments.
